extracted.intended_audience: prospective NSF proposers (PIs, co-PIs), research administrators, and NSF staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance covering NSF proposal preparation, submission, merit review criteria, award administration, financial and reporting requirements, and related policies for proposers and awardees across NSF programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of NSF Support / Ineligible Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF does not normally support technical assistance, pilot plant efforts, research requiring security classification, development of products for commercial marketing, or market research for a particular project or invention; research with disease-related goals (etiology, diagnosis, treatment of disease in humans or animals) is normally not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist for bioengineering or information technology research that applies engineering or computer science principles to biology/medicine while advancing engineering or computer science knowledge; bioengineering and assistive IT research to aid persons with disabilities also eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Submit Proposals / Categories of Proposers
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines eligible proposers including Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs), non-profit/non-academic organizations, for-profit organizations, state/local governments, unaffiliated individuals, foreign organizations, and other categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special instructions apply for international branch campuses of U.S. IHEs and other specific proposer categories; consult Exhibit II-3 for personnel categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Submit Proposals – Target Dates, Deadlines, Submission Windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies target dates, deadline dates, submission windows, and special exceptions to NSF’s deadline date policy (e.g., natural disasters, NSF closure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program solicitations and Divisional/Office websites also list deadline and target date information; follow special exception procedures when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates submission types such as Letters of Intent, Preliminary Proposals, Full Proposals, Invite/Not Invite, Encourage/Discourage, Group Proposals, Renewal Proposals, and special proposals (RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, GOALI, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual program solicitations may modify general provisions; special submission types have program-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with Instructions for Proposal Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must conform to the PAPPG instructions for preparation and submission including format, content, and required documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization to deviate must be explicitly requested where permitted; failure to conform may result in return without review or other processing actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of the Proposal (Pagination, Font, Spacing, Margin Requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies page formatting rules including pagination instructions and font, spacing and margin requirements for proposal documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict adherence is required; formatting deviations can affect page limits and may lead to noncompliance in processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary is a required section of proposals and must concisely describe the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary typically must address the overview and the two merit review criteria (Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts) in separate statements—follow program-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description — Content and Page Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description must contain the narrative description of the proposed activity and adhere to page limitations; it may include Results from Prior NSF Support where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of URLs within the Project Description is constrained by the PAPPG (see page limitation guidance); use appendices only where explicitly allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results from Prior NSF Support
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, proposals must include Results from Prior NSF Support describing prior NSF-funded work, outputs, and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific instructions for content and placement; this information is used by reviewers to assess productivity and stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include complete and properly formatted references cited for the project narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References should be sufficient for reviewers to locate and evaluate cited works; improper or incomplete citations can impede review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch(es) Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical sketches for senior personnel must include professional preparation, appointments, products, and synergistic activities as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow format and content rules in the PAPPG; required elements (a–d) must be present and adhere to page limits and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Personnel / Senior Personnel Definitions and Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines categories of personnel (senior personnel, other personnel) and specifies what must be included for each in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Exhibit II-3 for definitions and include required information accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include a detailed budget and budget justification covering salaries and wages, fringe benefits, equipment, travel, participant support, consultant services, computer services, subawards, and other direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NSF policies on senior personnel salaries & wages, administrative and clerical staff treatment, pre-award costs, prior written approvals, and confidential budgetary information rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of Costs (Allowable/Unallowable Items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes what costs are allowable or unallowable under NSF awards (examples include entertainment, meals, alcoholic beverages, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes policy on basic considerations, conflicting guidelines, maximum obligation, pre-award costs, post-end costs, and need for prior approvals for certain items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs (Facilities & Administrative (F&A) / Indirect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on indirect costs including NSF policy, cognizant organizations, and calculation/negotiation of indirect (F&A) costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of total direct and indirect costs, fee payments under NSF grants, and indirect cost rate negotiation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and expectations regarding cost sharing, including mandatory cost sharing commitments and records and reports where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail on when cost sharing is required and how it must be documented; mandatory commitments must be tracked and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and Pending Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must disclose current and pending support for senior personnel to allow assessment of available effort and overlap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and accurate disclosure is required; omissions or misrepresentations can affect award decisions and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must describe available facilities, equipment, and other resources that will support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions should be clear about access, adequacy, and institutional support; reviewers use this to assess feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans for Data Management and Sharing of the Products of Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include plans for data management and sharing of research products (data, software, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs must provide a data management plan consistent with NSF policy; absence or inadequate plans can affect merit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral Researcher Mentoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, proposals must include a mentoring plan for postdoctoral researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mentoring plan should describe training and professional development activities; certain solicitations require this explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of Collaborative Arrangements (Letters of Collaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative arrangements of significance must be documented in the proposal via letters of collaboration or similar documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should document the nature and extent of collaboration but must not be used to circumvent page limits or include cost commitments unless explicitly allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary or Privileged Information / Confidential Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on marking and handling proprietary or privileged information in proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PAPPG rules for identifying proprietary information; inappropriate marking or inclusion can affect processing or public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Suggested Reviewers or Reviewers Not to Include
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers may provide a list of suggested reviewers and/or reviewers they prefer not to include, subject to program rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF may consider suggestions but selection of reviewers is at NSF's discretion; conflicts of interest will be screened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Certifications and Collaborators & Other Affiliations Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include required certifications and complete Collaborators & Other Affiliations information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications are representations by the submitting organization and AOR; accurate collaborators/affiliations data is used for reviewer selection and COI screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes NSF's merit review principles governing fairness, transparency, and use of expert reviewers (see Chapter III).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merit review is carried out by Program Officers, Division Directors, and external reviewers; PIs receive unattributed verbatim copies of peer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: One of NSF’s two foundational merit review criteria—assesses the potential to advance knowledge and understanding within disciplines or across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate originality, conceptualization, methodology, and qualifications; proposals should explicitly address Intellectual Merit where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criteria: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The second foundational merit review criterion—assesses the potential to benefit society and contribute to desired societal outcomes (education, diversity, dissemination, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe how the project will promote broader impacts; reviewers consider quality, feasibility, and likely efficacy of Broader Impacts activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers and Conflict of Interest Screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for selection of reviewers and identification/handling of potentially disqualifying conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit II-2 lists potentially disqualifying conflicts; NSF follows policies to ensure fair and unbiased review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal File Updates and Revisions During Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing updates to the proposal file and permitted revisions to proposals during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant or substantive changes during review may require prior approval or withdrawal/resubmission; follow PAPPG procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Recommendation and NSF Risk Management Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes process for funding recommendations and the role of NSF's risk management framework in award decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF Program Officers recommend, with Grants Officers issuing awards; risk assessments and programmatic considerations factor into award/decline decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Instrument, Award Conditions, and Acceptance of Assistance Agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies types of award instruments (standard grant, continuing grant, cooperative agreement, fixed amount award) and NSF award conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award conditions incorporate relevant sections of the PAPPG by reference; cooperative agreements include terms describing substantial NSF involvement when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Responsibilities, Notifications to NSF, and Requests for NSF Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantee obligations during award performance include monitoring project progress, requesting NSF approvals for changes in scope/objectives, personnel changes, and reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include changes in PI/PD, significant changes in methods/procedures, addition of co-PIs, and long-term disengagement; prior approvals may be required for budgetary or scope changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Reporting Requirements and Public Project Outcomes Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must comply with technical reporting requirements such as Annual Project Reports, Final Project Report, and the Project Outcomes Report for the General Public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must be submitted per schedule and content guidance; compliance affects closeout and future award considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Financial Management, Payment Requirements, and Payment Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines financial management standards for grantees, procedures for requesting payments, advance payments, working capital advances, and grantee banking information requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes policy on erroneous payments, interest earned on advances, program income, and other cost credits; grantees must maintain appropriate financial systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Retention and Audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must retain records and be prepared for audits; CAAR performs cost analyses and audit resolution related to allowability and appropriateness of claimed costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements for accounting systems, indirect cost rate negotiation, and audit response procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Standards: Conflict of Interest and Responsible & Ethical Conduct of Research (RECR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on conflict of interest and institutional responsibilities for promoting responsible and ethical conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must have RECR training and oversight as appropriate; NSF responsibilities and expectations of grantees are described in the PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Living Organisms, Human Subjects, Vertebrate Animals, and DURC
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for proposals involving human subjects, vertebrate animals, recombinant/synthetic nucleic acid, and Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must follow applicable regulations (IRB/IACUC approvals, DURC policies) and provide required documentation and assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property: Patents, Inventions, and Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on patents, inventions, copyright, and special patent/copyright situations for NSF-funded work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes responsibilities for dissemination and protection of intellectual property consistent with Federal statute and award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and Sharing of Research Results / Publication Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF policy expects grantees to disseminate research results and make materials available; includes publication/distribution responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF Public Access Repository (NSF-PAR) and other dissemination policies apply; grantees remain responsible for preparing results for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Processing Instructions and Special Types of Proposals (e.g., RAPID, EAGER, SBIR/STTR, I-Corps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides special processing or solicitation-specific instructions for expedited, exploratory, technology translation, or other specialized programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow program solicitations for eligibility, submission deadlines, and program-specific requirements; these may modify general PAPPG provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Proposals, Group Proposals, and Subawarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for preparing collaborative/group proposals and policies for subawards and transfer of award segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document collaborative arrangements clearly, follow rules for subaward budgets and approvals, and adhere to institutional responsibilities for subaward oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Considerations: International Activities, Projects Requiring HPC or Major Instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and special requirements for proposals involving international activities, high-performance computing resources, data infrastructure, or advanced visualization resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documentation of international arrangements, resource requests, and any required approvals or institutional commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Administration Disputes, Suspension/Termination, and Research Misconduct Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for suspension and termination of awards, informal resolution of disputes, and reporting/handling of research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes definitions, NSF policies on misconduct reporting, role of grantees, and OIG investigative procedures.
